report:
The principal geometric construction and the strengthened birational loss-of-data example check out. The entire manuscript nevertheless fails the exact completion criterion because the generalized L1 continuity claim in Proposition 5.4 is false in its stated domain.

Concrete defect. The proposition says that, for states whose measures have support in a common compact affine set, total variation convergence of the measures implies local L1 convergence of their reconstructed primitives. It does not require convergence or constancy of the other state coordinates. Take D_j=(1,1,1,0,κ_j), with κ_j=0 for even j and κ_j=−1 for odd j. These are admissible states in the same big non-nef class; their measures are identically zero and therefore converge in total variation. Their reconstructed primitives are Φ_j=e+κ_j. On any compact coordinate region K outside E having positive volume, the even and odd subsequences differ by the constant one. Consequently Φ_j has no local L1 limit. The identity modification already supplies a counterexample. The explicit constants coordinate cannot be discarded: the manuscript retains actual primitives and exact pointwise order, rather than primitives modulo constants.

The proof establishes the valid kernel estimate ‖U_ν∘f−U_ν′∘f‖L1(K)≤C_K‖ν−ν′‖TV. For complete primitives the corresponding estimate additionally contains |a−a′|‖e∘p‖L1(K)+|κ−κ′|Vol(K). Thus fixed a and κ, or convergence of those coordinates, suffices. Adding those hypotheses narrows the asserted statement; I have not credited that amended statement with a PASS. The specific fixed-state approximation (5.4) has those coordinates fixed and is valid.

Kernel and admissibility. With the stated ddᶜ convention, ddᶜlog|z−t|²=δ_t and ddᶜlog(1+|z|²)=ω, with ∫ω=1. The difference between the denominator and numerator in the kernel ratio is |1+z t̄|², establishing G≤0. Uniform local logarithmic L1 bounds justify Fubini and ddᶜU_ν=ν−mω. Fatou gives upper semicontinuity, and integrated submean inequalities establish the canonical representative. The potential is smooth outside its support, including near infinity, and condition (2.2) makes its pole set exactly S. Its nontrivial local psh primitives establish that S is polar; local integrability also makes S area-null. Positive sums and positive scalings preserve admissibility, with the separately specified zero convention.

Exponential integrability and holomorphic pullback. Atomlessness permits restricted mass δ<1/h. Jensen reduces the local exponential estimate to an averaged kernel |z−t|^(−2hδ), whose area integral is finite because hδ<1. The complementary contribution is bounded after shrinking the disc. For a nonconstant holomorphic pullback, a direction detecting the first nonzero Taylor term gives finite order d. Argument-principle stability on both the outer and half-radius circles keeps exactly d roots inside the half-disc. Factoring these roots leaves a zero-free unit with a uniform positive lower bound: bound the numerator below and the root product above on the outer circle, then apply the maximum principle to the reciprocal unit. Hölder gives a uniform integral bound when dε<1; choosing δ<1/(hd) completes Jensen and Fubini. Holomorphic root selections are unnecessary. The same estimates control logarithmic L1 norms uniformly in the kernel parameter. The local primitives remain nontrivial because a nonconstant holomorphic scalar has open image whereas S has empty interior. This validates the new pullback lemma without a birational integrability grant.

Sector geometry and operations. The reconstructed current is positive because all displayed coefficients are nonnegative and the polar pullback is defined through actual psh primitives. The hyperplanes through the blown-up point generate its ideal, so their graph realizes the blowup as a closed subvariety of Y×P². Restricting the product Segre polarization proves that A=2(H_z+H_w)−E is ample. Decomposition (3.5) therefore supplies a Kähler current for every a,b,c>0. The intersections H_zE=H_wE=0 and E²=−1 give α_DE=−a<0, proving non-nefness. On a fixed leaf, every base point has a lift outside E, so the stated kernel order is exactly the order of the reconstructed primitives. Addition, positive scaling, constants and the zero-coefficient conventions are consistent. Fiber integration recovers (b−m)ω+ν; its area-singular part recovers ν. Envelope monotonicity, positive homogeneity and invariance under input constants follow directly from competitor inclusions and reindexing the ceiling parameter.

Modifications and references. For every given smooth proper bimeromorphic p:W→X, pulled sections retain the complete divisor p*E and all multiplicities. The holomorphic pullback lemma applies to q∘p, and the current identity and further-composition compatibility follow from the same local primitives. Extending ideals preserves sums, products and units, so the semivaluation pushforward composes and contracts supports correctly. Reference covariance (4.2) follows from the bijection v↦v−f between the transported competitor sets. Bounded metric changes preserve multiplier ideals. No topology identification of the enriched carrier with MP is established or used.

Ideals and nonpluripolar products. Near E, the polar term is smooth, and radial integration gives the exact threshold j+1>ta; this produces floor(ta), including integral values. Away from E, all exponential orders are integrable. On W, the polar term is bounded near p⁻¹E because that divisor maps to infinity; outside it the exceptional term is smooth and pullback exponential integrability applies. Hence I(tΦ_D∘p)=I(ta e∘p), without requiring an SNC divisor. The componentwise floor formula is asserted only in the SNC case. The asymptotic ideal profile is −a v(I_E), including supported semivaluations; eventual positive ideal powers avoid any 0·∞ arithmetic.

For products, the closed pole set is p⁻¹E∪(q∘p)⁻¹S and is locally complete pluripolar. Its complement current is the smooth form p*S_D. The inverse image of S is Lebesgue-null in submersion coordinates by Fubini. The remaining critical locus is contained locally in the zero set of a nonzero holomorphic derivative and is also Lebesgue-null. Thus all smooth coefficient measures vanish on the pole set. The finite complement-product criterion applies locally on W, without assuming W Kähler, and gives ⟨T_D,W^k⟩=(p*S_D)^k for k=1,2. Squaring the residue form gives the factor 2c(b−m); degree-one change of variables on the bimeromorphic isomorphism locus preserves its integral. These are genuine raw products and masses.

Approximation. For fixed D, the coefficients 1−1/j increase while U_ν≤0, so Φ_Dj decreases everywhere to Φ_D, including its poles. The total variation error is m/j. The residue products converge through their explicit smooth polynomial formulas, and the masses are 2c(b−m+m/j). Uniform kernel L1 bounds extend to every fixed modification by the factorization estimate and finite local covers. These statements hold; they do not establish the broader primitive-continuity assertion contradicted above.

Cantor supports and envelope separation. The endpoint intervals are disjoint, their lengths tend to zero, and the Bernoulli cylinder masses establish both full support and atomlessness. At each support point, U_μ0≤−2·2^j for every j; the translated construction has the same bound. The two supports are disjoint. Their maximum is bounded because the other potential is smooth near either support. It is nonconstant: upper semicontinuity creates an ordinary open region near a support point where the other smooth potential wins and has Hessian −ω. For ν_i=sμ_i, the entire real-scale ideal families and both nonpluripolar products coincide on every given smooth modification, with positive mass 2c(b−s). Their maximum differs boundedly from ae. Applying premises 1 and 3 in the verified compact Kähler, big-class, canonical and positive-mass domain gives the contradiction 2bc≤2c(b−s)<2bc if their normalized ordinary envelopes coincide. This establishes different ordinary P-envelopes without assuming envelope/max commutation. At a=s=1/2 and b=c=1, the first product, top measure, mass one and self-intersection 7/4 are all correct.

Application of B. Negative restriction degree forces the full exceptional factor in each cleared section degree. The residual sections descend: in the affine charts of Y, a rational coefficient with a denominator factor would have a surviving divisorial pole away from the blown-up point. The generated residual bundle is therefore A=π*O(b,c), with actual fixed factor T=aE. For varying incoming bundles B_i, the exceptional coefficient is at least ceil(−ℓ B_i·E); hence its normalized lower bound tends to a. Incoming generic constants tend to zero, giving the required divisorial inequality, and B's all-point order determination promotes it everywhere. Thus q_T is the normalized reference. The stationary moving model has A²=2bc and C³=3d(2bc), giving auxiliary energy zero and raw measure 2bc δ_v0 with central multiplicity one. The horizontal factor aE remains retained. All applications stay within B's granted actual-big rational projective trivially valued characteristic-zero domain. Neither internal G0/G1 nor B's other domains were treated as separate grants. No complex-to-NA operator identification follows.

Primary evidence and note audit. I independently opened the literal [BEGZ v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2) and [DDL v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.05796v3) sources and read the pertinent complete units: BEGZ §1.2 through Proposition 1.6; DDL Theorems 2.3/2.4, the §3.2 membership argument and Theorem 3.12. For the optional weak-convergence conclusion in premise 2, the limsup-mass hypothesis itself supplies a uniform mass bound; no ordinary non-nef self-intersection bound is needed. All mathematical fields of n1–n3 were checked against the reconstructed argument. Hashes, compilation reports, author labels and previous verdict descriptions supplied no mathematical evidence. B is a task grant, separately documented below without an external-premise index; it is not a registered native-note support ID.

Harmless clarifications are that ‘area zero’ on W means ambient Lebesgue-nullness, and L1 differences are taken almost everywhere rather than subtracting infinite values at common poles. The missing coordinate hypotheses in the generalized L1 assertion are a substantive scope correction.

The established partial scope is this prescribed-fibration analytic sector on Bl_(∞,∞)(P¹×P¹), with admissible diffuse polar measures, its stated geometric operations, fixed-state decreasing approximation, compatibility on every given smooth modification, and the strengthened specified-tower obstruction. It does not close original P14.4. Arbitrary compact Kähler manifolds, genuinely transcendental/nonprojective big non-nef classes, arbitrary P-type realization, maximum closure, PL/model approximation, compatible DXZ/MP realization and common-domain operator comparisons remain unproved here. The bounded nonconstant maximum explicitly witnesses failure of maximum closure in the sector. The obstruction concerns the specified ideal/nonpluripolar tower, not every possible movable datum. No P14.5/P14.6 theory or other original atom is solved.

passages.statement: BEGZ, arXiv:0812.3674v2, §1.2, Definitions 1.1/1.2 and Propositions 1.4/1.6: On a complex n-manifold, for 1≤p≤n and local psh potentials u_j, the locally finite nonpluripolar product is determined by the increasing currents 1_{∩j{u_j>−N}}∧j ddᶜmax(u_j,−N), depends only on the currents, is plurifine-local and charges no pluripolar set. If all potentials are locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set A, it is well-defined exactly when the complement Bedford–Taylor product has locally finite mass near A; it is then its trivial extension. Products of closed positive (1,1)-currents on compact Kähler manifolds are well-defined.
